arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Amgen's counsel stated that claiming a lot while enabling a little short-changes the public.
Amgen's counsel argued that Sanofi failed to identify any antibody requiring undue experimentation.
Sanofi's counsel noted that scientists do not use the patented method if an antibody already exists.
Justice Sotomayor questioned why Amgen had not made a specific antibody if the process was easy.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case centers on the scope of a patent claim. Amgen holds a patent for antibodies that bind to a specific spot on the PCSK9 protein. Sanofi argues this claim is too broad. Amgen argues the claim is valid because it teaches a general method to find such antibodies.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between a valid patent claim and an overbroad one. It determines how much specific detail a patent must provide when claiming a large class of molecules. The outcome affects the balance between rewarding invention and keeping scientific knowledge accessible.
